newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine phone firms slip on land lines target.
newsitem.headline: Philippine phone firms slip on land lines target.

text.p: Nine Philippine telecommunications firms have installed 365,121 telephone lines for the first six months of this year, 91 percent of their 401,795 line targets for the period, an official said.

National Telecommunications Commission head Simeon Kintanar told reporters on Monday the nine firms under the government's service area scheme renewed their promise to install a total of 5.69 million telephone lines within the mandated three year period or by 1998.
"The slippage is only nine percent and all of them are coming up with catch-up programmes within the year," he said.
The Philippines had granted these companies licences to run lucrative cellular phone businesses on condition they install a minimum number of land lines.
Of the nine companies, Philippine Long Distance Telephone Co, ICC Telecoms and Smart Communications Inc are ahead of schedule.

PLDT installed 124,053 lines of its 120,340 target while ICC Telecoms laid 135,567 lines of its 99,860 target. Smart was able to put up 110 lines. It is slated to start its roll-out plan late this year.
Major Telecoms Inc and Pilipino Telephone Corp will start line installation by the end of the year.

Companies which are suffering delays in the roll-out plans are Digital Telecommunications Philippines Inc having installed 27,296 lines of its 46,010 target; Globe Telecom GMCR Inc with 56,811 lines of its 81,489 target; Philippine Telegraph & Telephone Corp with 21,000 lines of 50,000 target and Isla Communications Co Inc with 284 lines of its 4,096 committed lines to be installed for the first six months of this year.
